top.title: 9 Calvin and Hobbes Comics from the 1990s that Prove Bill Watterson is a Genius
top.description: Calvin and Hobbes creator Bill Watterson is a genius . Over the course of ten years spanning more than 3,000 comic strips , he developed two truly irresistible characters that are still beloved by millions. There was a lot behind the success of Calvin and Hobbes , but I think part of the reason why Watterson is still so widely respected is that he was an incredibly versatile artist who managed to do a lot of different things in an artform that can sometimes be limiting.

top.title: Masuk girls volleyball pushes past East Lyme, wins first CIAC title in five-set thriller
top.description: Masuk's Grace Morrow (2) cries tears of happiness as she celebrates with teammate Mia Tyler (5) following their 3-2 win over East Lyme to capture the the Class L volleyball state championship Friday, November 20, 2026 at Bulkeley High School in Hartford. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) HARTFORD - The third-seeded Masuk girls volleyball team went from a two-set lead to a fifth-set, winner-take-all battle in the CIAC Class L state championship match against top-seeded East Lyme on Friday night. The Panthers, who fell behind by three points early in that fifth set, dug deep, came back and dethroned the defending champion Vikings, 3-2, to win their first state championship. The set scores were 25-21, 25-20, 24-26, 27-29, 15-10. Senior captain Mia Tyler, who won MVP honors when Masuk captured its first South-West Conference championship earlier this month, was named Class L's most outstanding player. The Panthers finished 24-2 while the Vikings ended their season at 20-5. East Lyme held a 21-19 lead in the first set, but Masuk scored the final six points to strike first. Panther senior Jacqueline Silkman had a key tip during that run to give her team a 22-21 lead. Another tip by senior captain Grace Morrow ended the set in Masuk's favor. The second set was much the same as East Lyme ran out to an early lead, only to see Masuk come back ayet again. The Panthers finally caught up at 16-16, then the set was even again at 18-18 before the No. 3 seed made their push. At 24-20, Masuk, an East Lyme hit was out long to give the Panthers a 2-0 lead in the match. East Lyme ran out to an 8-3 lead in the third set, but stayed in control this time until Masuk caught them at 12-12. Trailing 15-14, Viking senior Natalie Knowlton scored six straight points, including five kills, for a 20-15 lead for the No. 1 seed. The Panthers came back to tie the set, 24-24, on a kill by junior Grace Kehoe. East Lyme senior Bella Albert had a block to put her team up 25-24, then sophomore Emma Knowlton's serve was not returned for a 26-24 set victory. The Vikings had hope, but the Panthers almost put them away in a frantic fourth set. Masuk owned two six-point leads, 14-8 and 21-15, but East Lyme ripped off six straight points to tie the set, 21-21, the last point coming on a Emma Knowlton kill. The Panthers took a 23-21 lead, only to watch the Vikings score three straight points to earn a set point at 24-23. An East Lyme hitting error and a Masuk ace by freshman Skylar Tengeres gave her team a match point, 25-24. A 31-second point went in favor of the Vikings on an Emma Knowlton kill to tie the set, 25-25. East Lyme senior Savannah Marusov served an ace for a 26-25 lead, but a net violation call tied the set again, 26-26. A Viking block made it 27-26, but Panther senior captain Addison Scott rocketed a hit through blockers to tie it again, 27-27. top.title: 5 takeaways from Oregon Ducks stylish 45-7 blowout over Michigan State
top.description: It was a game that the Oregon Ducks needed to win, and needed to look good doing so. They did just that. Dan Lanning's team got its first ever victory in East Lansing on Friday night, beating the Michigan State Spartans 45-7 in a game that really was ugly early on, but dominated in the second half. Spurred on by a fake field goal that went for a touchdown right before the break, Oregon scored 35 points over the final 30 minutes and seven seconds of the game, and put up some style points in the eyes of the College Football Playoff committee, which may have been the most important outcome of it all. The defense was dominant once again, while true freshman running back Brandon Smith stepped in for an injured Dierre Hill and had a coming-out party. Now, with a full day of college football ahead of us on Saturday, we will sit back and see how things unfold for the Ducks . Before that, though, here are our biggest takeaways from the game: Style Points Coming into this game, there was a notion that winning wasn't going to be enough for Oregon; the Ducks needed to win with style. Sitting on the outside of the College Football Playoff field looking in, an impressive showing was needed in order to help convince the committee that Oregon is playing as one of the best 12 teams in the nation right now, and deserving of a shot at the national championship. I think they accomplished that. It didn't look pretty for much of the first two quarters, with Oregon putting up only 166 yards and 10 points before a gutsy fake field goal at the end of the half. But over the final 30 minutes and seven seconds of football, the Ducks were dominant. They ended up with 422 total yards and 45 points, letting some of their most dynamic players — mainly RB Brandon Smith and WR Dakorien Moore — show what they could do while the defense was dominant once again. A lot of things can happen in order to clear the Ducks' path to the playoffs, and we may see some of them come to fruition on Saturday, but even if some upsets don't take place, there's a reason to believe that Oregon might be able to get in at 9-3. Games like this one certainly help build the case. The Brandon Smith Game Without Dierre Hill for a majority of this game (more on that later), this quickly turned into the Brandon Smith game for the Ducks. Oregon fans knew before this game that they had something special in the true freshman, but he cemented that fact in this one, rushing 14 times for 121 yards and two touchdowns. It wasn't just the stats, but the way that he ran, shifting through contact, maintaining elite balance, and dancing down the sideline on impressive big gains. He looked good enough to get legendary Oregon RB Jonathan Stewart to make this statement: "Brandon Smith the best back in a Oregon jersey since Kenjon Barner." — @Jonathanstewar1 https://t.co/lxrIEzV7QT — Zachary Neel (@zacharycneel) November 21, 2026 Whether you agree with Stewart or not is beside the point. It's impossible to deny at this point

top.title: Instant Recap: Michigan State gets stomped by Oregon
top.description: Michigan State’s Derrick Simmons, left, tackles Oregon’s Da'Jaun Riggs during the first quarter on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026 in East Lansing. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Whew, boy. That was the worst loss of the season. It was all Oregon tonight. Michigan State’s offense struggled early, and Oregon scored halfway through the first quarter to give the Ducks a 7-0 lead behind a Brandon Smith 5-yard touchdown run. Frederick Moore had a nice one-handed snag right before the second quarter started, but Liam Boyd would miss a 47-yard field goal for Michigan State’s first chance to put points on the board. The offense was starting to look solid behind Kayd Coffman’s play, but he would trip while running out of the pocket to turn the ball over on a 4th-and-3 from Oregon’s 28-yard line. The defense did their best to keep the Spartans close, but their special teams did not. Chrishon McCray would muff the next punt by the Ducks to allow Oregon to take over in the redzone. The defense held tough and forced them to kick a field goal, and it made it a 10-0 game. Near the end of the first half, Dan Lanning called a fake field goal where the Ducks’ kicker was able to run it in from 15 yards out to give Oregon a 17-0 lead heading into halftime. Once that fake field goal scored, it felt like the game was already out of reach. Oregon opened up the second half with another touchdown run, this time from Simeon Price, to put them up 24-0. Michigan State would respond with a touchdown of their own with a direct snap from the 1-yard line by Jaz Patterson, though it would be the only points they scored all night. Both Brandon Smith and Simeon Price would add another touchdown run each for the Ducks, and Dylan Raiola found Dakorien Moore for a nice one-handed touchdown pass as Oregon continued to pile on the points. Oregon would go on to win 45 to 7. Michigan State moves to 3-8 Kayd Coffman completed 10 of his 19 passes for 106 yards and one interception. Jaz Patterson handled 16 carries, but only managed 26 yards. Brandon Tullis added 25 yards on eight carries. The Spartans’ leading receiver was Fredrick Moore with 31 yards on two catches. It was a brutal loss, and one of those games where you wish it could’ve ended by the end of the third quarter, as Oregon kept putting more and more points on the scoreboard. Luckily for the Spartans, it’s not the end of the season, and they’ll finish it off with a matchup at Rutgers on Thanksgiving weekend. Let’s hope they can finish the season with a win. Go Green!

top.title: Couch: 3 quick takes on Michigan State football's 45-7 loss to Oregon
top.description: MSU battles as best it can against Oregon. That won't be acceptable against Rutgers. EAST LANSING — There are levels to this sport. And Oregon is on a different level than Michigan State right now. To MSU’s credit, the gap wasn’t as severe for parts of the night as it looked like it might be out of the gate, or as it appeared at the end on the scoreboard. I don’t know what does for MSU at this point, knowing you hung in there for a while and landed a few blows of your own in a 45-7 loss. It’s something to take into next week and into the offseason as you evaluate the roster, I guess. The Spartans ’ defense is playing some good football at times. MSU’s offense had some moments of life with young Kayd Coffman under center. For it to mean anything, they’ve got to beat Rutgers, the wet basement of the Big Ten. There are no moral victories next week in Piscataway. MSU wore down Friday night. The Spartans looked like a pesky Mid-American Conference team, with a few playmakers who belonged on the stage, playing a Big Ten team, with too much talent and depth. It’s a story as old as time. It’s just getting old that it’s sometimes MSU on the other end of these games. Oregon is fighting for a place in the College Football Playoff, a three-loss team that needs to impress a committee that appears to be in bed in the SEC. Hence the deep passes with a 38-7 lead. MSU is now an eight-loss team, trying to keep its chin up all the way to the finish line. If the Spartans’ special teams — their strength all season — hadn’t played their worst game by a mile, this final score might have been more indicative of the actual chasm between the programs, something like 31-10. That’s not exactly heartwarming. But that’s what this game was essentially — a 31-10 home loss to a program that’s where the Spartans want to be in terms for resources and year-over-year winning. And November stakes. This game was, at the very least, instructive. For this MSU season, next week is a bigger deal. You can’t lose three straight to close the season, including at Rutgers, and feel good going into a massive offseason, even with the win over Michigan. You’ve got to get one more W, and show that you’re not in the same realm as Rutgers. 2. Coffman shows improvement from his last start There is no question that freshman Kayd Coffman has some ability. You can see the lively arm and good feet. He’s at his best right now when they roll him outside of the pocket. top.title: MSU hockey falls at Michigan, suspensions coming after 3rd-period brawl
top.description: Lansing State Journal sports reporter Nathaniel Bott breaks down No. 9 Michigan State's 5-1 loss to No. 1 Michigan on Friday, Nov. 20 at Yost Ice Arena in Ann Arbor. What happened MSU came into Friday night looking to rebound after a two-point weekend at Notre Dame, facing off with rival Michigan for the only time in Ann Arbor this year, at least for the regular season. THE BIG PICTURE: MSU hockey looks to jump-start season with rivalry test against No. 1 Michigan The Spartans got off to a slow start, allowing a goal in the first six minutes while the Wolverines registered the first 11 shots on target. U-M would make it 2-0 on a goal from freshman forward J.P. Hurlbert (a 2026 Detroit Red Wings draft pick) with just over eight minutes remaining in the first period to bring the crowd back alive. The Spartans would get one back in the dying moments of the first period, with freshman Jack Hextall winning an offensive zone face-off back to freshman defenseman Tommy Bleyl, who then fed the puck down low back to Hextall, who delivered a pass through the U-M crease. Forward Cullen Potter, who shifted to the wing for the first time this season Friday, was there to jam the puck past goaltender Jack Ivankovic with just 21 seconds left in the first period to give the Spartans some momentum. MSU carried that into the second period, outshooting U-M 16-6 with multiple solid chances, but Ivankovic stood firm. U-M would later get a 3-on-1 rush the other way, and defenseman Asher Barnett beat MSU goaltender Joshua Ravensbergen to restore U-M's two-goal lead. The Wolverines would score twice more early in the third period, and then the fireworks began. MSU sophomore defenseman Sean Barnhill laid a big hit on U-M forward Nick Moldenhauer at the Michigan blue line, sparking a big scrum with Barnhill getting a two-minute minor for boarding and each side receiving matching roughing calls. With things seemingly settled down, MSU senior defenseman Patrick Geary went over to the U-M bench, sparking a number of Wolverine players to react and prompted all three MSU players to leave the penalty box and start the brawl again. Fireworks in the third period, Michigan up 5-1 and havoc at the bench pic.twitter.com/kyr0EvrgV1 — Max Bultman (@m_bultman) November 21, 2026 This time, however, the officials handed out multiple fighting majors, which carry a minimum one-game suspension. In total, U-M's Drew Schock, Michael Hage and Nic Sima, as well as MSU's Barnhill, forward Shane Vansaghi and defenseman Matt Lahey all received that penalty and will be suspended for Saturday's game, at minimum. Additional discipline could be handed out by the Big Ten after reviewing the incident. Ravensbergen made 33 saves for the Spartans, who fall to 6-4-1 on the season. Ivankovic stopped 37 MSU shots, as the Wolverines improve to 11-1. top.title: Jaguars score early, shut out nationally ranked Sals for soccer title
top.description: FREDERICA – Appoquinimink scored just four minutes into the DIAA Division I Boys Soccer Tournament final. In a sport where goals are rare and very difficult to get, it was a sweet and satisfying start. It also meant perennial powerhouse Salesianum, ranked 15 th in the nation, had the added incentive to score and 86 minutes in which to do it. The Sals could not, and Appoquinimink won a state championship that will long be as cherished and coveted as such accomplishments can be Nov. 20 at DE Turf. Freshman Caiden Stone scored that fourth-minute goal and the Jaguars spent the rest of the game thwarting one Salesianum opportunity after another, including two in the final minute alone. “It was just everybody,” senior captain and center back Gabriel Arbuet said. “Everybody worked their tails off. Last game of the season. Seniors especially, last game of their careers. “We just worked hard the whole entire time. We knew what was on the line. We knew we could make history. It was a whole team effort.” Third-seeded Appoquinimink (16-1) was playing in its sixth state boys soccer championship game, all since 2013, every one against Salesianum. The Jaguars prevailed in only one of those, the 2020 final on a tie-breaking penalty-kick shootout, which was their last title-game appearance. “We had a game plan going into it,” Appo coach Lance Berry said. “We worked on it the past two days and the boys executed perfectly. “So hats off to Sallies. They're a hell of a program. They're the standard. But our boys showed up tonight. Really proud of each and every guy.” Top-seeded Salesianum (15-3), its national ranking courtesy of the United Soccer Coaches, had beaten Appo 2-1 on Oct. 22. But both teams had conceded afterward that, with Appo missing three starters that night, a rematch might be even more competitive. It most certainly was, especially with the determination Salesianum gained with that early deficit. But the Sals, who’d won 20 of the last 24 state soccer titles and were appearing in their 17 th straight title game, couldn’t level the match despite numerous opportunities. Sometimes, perhaps out of a sense of desperation, they may have unleashed shots too early and from too far away rather than working for something better. Berry was happy to point out that the Jaguars set a school record with their 13 th shutout, having won all three state tournament games 1-0. They allowed five goals all year. “The defense has been lights out all year,” said Berry. “To be honest with you, I'm not too surprised . . . When we had all of our guys healthy, they have given up maybe a goal when they're all on the field.” Berry has now won boys and girls state titles as coach at both his alma mater Caravel and Appo. He again joined his dad John, who steered McKean to the 1984 title and was in attendance, on the list of championship coaches. top.description: JACKSONVILLE | He trudged through Duval County mud and across the goal lines adjacent to Moncrief Road to history four times, and Brian Wilson Jr. couldn't remember the last night that felt anything like that. "Maybe Little League?" the Miami Columbus running back guessed. The first-ever Florida High School Athletic Association Open Division game ever played within Jacksonville city limits was a winner for Wilson. But not for the home crowd, or the hometown champions. Watch Florida high school playoffs live on NFHS Network Got a great play? How to submit your high school sports highlights to the Times-Union Fueled on offense by Wilson's four touchdowns, and stifling the reigning state champions from start to finish, Miami Columbus closed the door on Raines' Open Division hopes and downed the Vikings 28-6 on Nov. 20 at the Graveyard. For the first time in six years, the 2025 state champion Vikings (10-2) have lost consecutive games, after going down 28-7 at West Boca Raton on Nov. 13 in the round-robin Open Division format. A gritty effort from a depleted Raines defense wasn't enough against the Explorers (11-1), who frustrated the Vikings throughout a night of wind-driven tropical downpours. But to end in the win column, Columbus needed the four scores from Wilson, the sophomore power back splitting carries with Northern Illinois-bound senior Cecil Smith. "After four touchdowns," Wilson said, "I feel amazing right now." top.title: Berlin football holds off Middletown, clinches its 5th straight playoff berth
top.description: Berlin's Gamaliel Ayizano, 4, tries to push his way past Middletown's Juel Ocasio, 54, during the CIAC football game between Middletown and Berlin high schools.Friday, November 20, 2026, Sage Park, Berlin, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media) BERLIN - The Berlin Redcoats are in. If there's any justice in the football world, the Middletown Blue Dragons will also qualify for the postseason, because on Friday night at Sage Park both teams showed they belong there. In a Central Connecticut Conference game played six nights before Thanksgiving, but befitting the playoff stage that will follow the holiday, Berlin clipped Middletown 35-32 to beat its neighbor to the south and qualify for the CIAC tournament for a fifth straight year. This baby was by far the closest of the five. What appeared to be a TKO when Berlin scored on the third play of the game and then recovered a fumble on Middletown's first snap instead turned into a 15-rounder that wasn't over until Berlin junior wide receiver Anthony Frayler secured an onside kick with 37 seconds left. Both teams scored five touchdowns. Both teams finished 7-3. The difference lay in Berlin junior Noah Foster going 5-for-5 on extra points and Berlin's defense stopping Middletown on all but one 2-point conversion try. A 31-yard touchdown run by Foster, coming with 1:56 left out of Berlin's new-wrinkle Wildcat, proved to be the game-winning score. Middletown, which had hung tough behind touchdown jaunts of 75, 15 and 60 yards by junior running back Nick Cyril, answered that Foster score to keep hope alive. Junior QB Matteo Fletcher, coming on early in the second half when starter Brendin Smith went down with an injury, hit senior Sebastiano Bibisi with a 38-yard pass on a fourth-and-10, then rifled a 12-yard TD pass over the middle to senior Victor Bonet. Berlin stuffed the 2-point run, then recovered the ensuing onside. And with that, last year's Class M state champ clinched a berth in the Class SS playoffs. Middletown remains in the top eight in Class MM at 7-3 and will secure a berth if any of the 6-3 teams on its heels - Fairfield Prep, Platt and Torrington - lose their regular-season finale next week. Even if all three win, Middletown might still get in on bonus points. On Friday night, the Redcoats drew opening blood on a 43-yard TD run by junior Brandon Sadowski on toss-right out of the double-wing. Also for Berlin, senior running back Gamaliel Ayizano broke off a 62-yard scoring dash straight up the middle, Frayler corralled a 30-yard TD pass down the right sideline from junior QB Chace Hrubiec and junior RB Nick Balicki muscled in a crucial score late in the first half on fourth down from the 1 after Middletown had made three stops inside the 3. The Blue Dragons got on the board via a 60-yard pick-six from Bibisi. Foster and Sadowski had interceptions for Berlin. Junior Liam DeSantos had the fumble recovery on Middletown's first snap. top.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Peru
top.description: A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities. The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers. Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.” Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.” AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake. The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao. Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.” Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.” Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire — an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them. A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes. top.title: Darian DeVries wants the Indiana-Kentucky rivalry series to continue
top.description: Nov 20, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indiana Hoosiers head coach Darian DeVries looks for an intentional foul against the Kentucky Wildcats during the second half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A lot has changed from when Indiana and Kentucky agreed to resume their longstanding annual rivalry series in men’s basketball. Darian DeVries took over as head coach for the Hoosiers ahead of the first matchup in the 2025-26 season, which was Mark Pope’s second year as the head coach of the Wildcats. Neither was in their position when the series was agreed upon, with Mike Woodson and John Calipari leading their respective programs at the time. Resuming the series was a priority for Woodson, who took a game at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis rather than Assembly Hall in Bloomington to get it done. top.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Illinois started the season with a bang, making the most three-pointers in a game in program history in the 120-45 win over FDU. Just seconds later, Ethan Brown hit his seventh three from beyond the arc to bring the team’s total to 21. top.description: EAST LANSING – Depleted at quarterback. Banged-up at running back. Out of bodies at linebacker. All of the injuries finally caught up to Michigan State football . And there was nothing the Spartans could do – no matter how hard they competed and fought through them – to stop No. 14 Oregon. nigeria.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Peru
nigeria.description: A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities. The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers. Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.” Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.” AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake. The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao. Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.” Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.” Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire — an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them. A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes. nigeria.title: Why obesity hits men harder than women – Study
nigeria.description: By Shola Ogundipe Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological difference in the fat tissue of males and females that could help explain why obesity triggers different health consequences in men and women. The discovery suggests that the battle against obesity may be playing out differently beneath the skin, with immune cells living inside body fat either helping to protect against inflammation and metabolic disorders or making them worse, depending on biological sex. Researchers at the University of California, Riverside, US, found that a group of immune cells known as eosinophils, traditionally associated with allergies and asthma, perform different functions in the fat tissue of male and female mice. While certain populations of these cells appear to protect against obesity-related inflammation, others may contribute to harmful metabolic changes. The study, titled “Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity”, was funded by the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine. The findings, published in the journal PNAS Nexus, challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar in structure and function. They also raise questions about whether obesity treatments targeting the immune system should be designed differently for men and women. Led by biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik, the study used high-resolution single-cell sequencing to examine how individual immune cells behave in fat tissue. What emerged was an unexpected picture. The researchers identified six distinct populations of eosinophils in adipose tissue, each with its own genetic activity and potentially different biological functions. The discovery suggests that these cells are not simply passive occupants of body fat. Some may help maintain metabolic health, while others may contribute to the inflammatory processes associated with obesity. “Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought,” said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences at UCR’s School of Medicine. She explained that identifying and activating the biological pathways responsible for producing protective eosinophils could open new possibilities for improving metabolic health. But perhaps the most striking finding was the difference between male and female mice. Female mice had a population of eosinophils that appeared to work more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells found in fat tissue. Their cooperation seemed to support a healthier environment within fat tissue and better metabolic function. Male mice, however, showed a different response when exposed to a high-fat diet. They were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation, alongside weaker protective activity in their fat tissue. nigeria.title: Delta: Six suspects in custody, no justice yet for Adeda?
nigeria.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi From a workplace assault to justice in limbo, family grief and fears deepen 58 days after death of a Delta State Deputy Director. Fifty-eight days after Unity Ekwevugbe Adeda died following a brutal workplace assault in Asaba, Delta State, six suspects remain in police custody, but no charges have been filed and no autopsy conducted to establish precise medical cause of death. For the Adeda family of Otovwodo, Ughelli, the prolonged wait for answers is deepening their grief and fears that those responsible for the death of their son could escape justice. Adeda, a Level 16 Deputy Director in the Department of Examination and Standards, Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education, died on September 24, 2026, following a physical altercation at his workplace. His death triggered protests by civil servants. It led to the constitution of an administrative panel of inquiry by the Delta State Government. The police also commenced separate criminal investigation. But nearly two months after the incident, the family and concerned stakeholders are asking what progress has been made towards prosecution. Six Suspects, No Charges The police investigation, handled by the Homicide Section of the State Criminal Investigation Department, has resulted in six arrests, including Dr. Kingsley Ashibogwu, Commissioner for Secondary Education, and Mrs Clementine Ufuoma, Director of Basic and Secondary Education. The arrests began with Lucky Adoh, an aide to the commissioner, shortly after the incident. Ashibogwu and three other suspects were subsequently taken into custody, bringing the number to five. Ufuoma, earlier declared wanted, later surrendered, increasing the number to six. Despite the arrests, no formal charges have been announced. Under the criminal justice process, the police are expected to conclude investigations, compile their findings and forward the duplicate case file to the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP), Ministry of Justice, for legal advice. The DPP is expected to examine the evidence and determine whether a prima facie case exists to warrant formal charges. However, the process has yet to reach that stage publicly, leaving questions about when the investigation will be concluded. For Austine Aghomi, Coordinator, Journalists for Just Development of the Niger Delta, the silence of the police and the delay in providing meaningful updates are increasingly troubling. He said: “But more concerning is the arrested progress on the part of the police. When will investigations be concluded? “Can’t prosecution progress with a few other suspects still at large? Where is the autopsy to determine or confirm Adeda’s true cause of death after the assault? “The police have not helped this case at all and it is just another test of integrity, seeing the police mum on this case for so long without offering meaningful updates. “It’s like a conspiracy theory is building over this matter. nigeria.title: No roof for two masters, by Stephanie Shaakaa
nigeria.description: * Bloodline, Ballot Box, and the Bedroom: Lessons from Kano’s High Stakes Political Divorce A marriage rarely belongs to two people alone. In northern Nigeria, where zumunci binds families through kinship, mutual obligations and family honour, marriage often carries expectations that extend far beyond the couple. For twenty years, the union between Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and Zainab Musa Kwankwaso appeared to demonstrate that bloodline and political loyalty could coexist under one roof. Today, that roof has given way. The breakdown of the marriage between Governor Yusuf and Zainab, niece of his estranged political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and raised in the former governor’s household, is more than a headline from Government House. It raises an uncomfortable question: what happens when the political alliance connecting two families collapses, but the marriage binding them is left caught in its aftermath? To understand the significance of this separation, one must understand how political trust is built in Kano. Political relationships are not always sustained by ambition and party loyalty alone. Sometimes, they are reinforced through family connections. When Zainab and Abba Yusuf married on July 29, 2006, Yusuf was already deeply embedded in Kwankwaso’s political circle, having served as his personal and special assistant during Kwankwaso’s first tenure as governor and subsequently during his tenure as Minister of Defence. Zainab, raised in Kwankwaso’s household, was not simply marrying an ambitious politician. Their union connected two families whose fortunes were closely intertwined. Over twenty years and six children, the marriage became one of the most personal bonds surrounding the Kwankwasiyya movement. Yusuf’s years of loyalty and proximity to Kwankwaso eventually culminated in his emergence as the latter’s preferred successor and his election as governor in 2023. The trusted lieutenant had become governor, with the backing of the political establishment that had shaped his career. Yet there is a particular difficulty with marriages surrounded by powerful family and political networks. The expectations attached to them can become difficult to separate from the personal commitments of the couple. While everyone shares the same interests, the arrangement may appear harmonious. The real test comes when those interests begin to diverge. That divergence became unmistakable in January 2026, when Governor Yusuf abandoned the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), the platform on which he won office, and defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The decision marked a decisive break with Kwankwaso, the political mentor who had nurtured his rise. nigeria.title: Do women control their husbands?
nigeria.description: By Chioma Gabriel, Editor, Special Features It is often said that women are a necessary evil, a desirable calamity and a domestic peril. It all depends on where one is standing. In traditional African societies, a woman’s place was said to be in the kitchen, from where she was expected to work her way into her husband’s heart through his stomach. Women were traditionally expected to be seen but not heard. They were like shadows trailing their husbands, with little or no opportunity to express opinions on matters affecting the family and society. They were often regarded as acquired possessions whose primary responsibilities were to bear children and provide labour on the farms. They had little or no say in the scheme of things. A similar pattern appears in some biblical accounts, where headcounts excluded women and children. When Jesus fed the 5,000 and the 4,000, the recorded figures referred to the men, with women and children excluded from the count. In the early Christian community, Paul’s instruction required women to remain silent in church and ask their husbands questions at home. Although interpretations of this passage differ among Christian scholars, it has historically been cited to support restrictions on women’s public religious participation. Despite these historical and cultural limitations, women have, in different ways, exercised considerable influence over men, including their husbands. Biblical accounts The Bible contains several accounts of women whose actions, decisions or influence significantly shaped the lives of men. Eve persuaded Adam to eat the forbidden fruit after the serpent tempted her in the Garden of Eden. Jezebel manipulated her husband, King Ahab, and orchestrated the murder of Naboth to acquire his vineyard. Delilah used persistent pressure and deception to make Samson reveal the secret of his extraordinary strength. Sapphira conspired with her husband, Ananias, to deceive the apostles about the proceeds from the sale of their property. Michal helped David escape from King Saul but later confronted and despised him over his public dancing before God. Bathsheba, working alongside the prophet Nathan, intervened to ensure that David fulfilled his promise that Solomon would succeed him as king. Sarah persuaded Abraham to have a child through her maidservant, Hagar, and later demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away. Rebekah orchestrated a family deception by persuading her son Jacob to disguise himself as Esau and obtain Isaac’s blessing. Herodias influenced her daughter to demand the head of John the Baptist from her husband, Herod Antipas. Job’s wife, overwhelmed by their suffering, urged her husband to curse God and die. Mary and Martha also demonstrated the emotional influence women could have. When their brother, Lazarus, died, their grief deeply moved Jesus, who wept before raising him from the dead. nigeria.title: Infantino hails Warri Stadium, wants football in every community
nigeria.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has praised the renovated Warri City Stadium in Delta State, saying football development must extend beyond major stadiums to local communities. Infantino spoke during a visit to Warri, where he attended the commissioning of the renovated stadium and upgraded sporting facilities. The FIFA president said football should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their location, adding that smaller stadiums play an important role in bringing the sport closer to communities. “Yeah, that’s what football is about, isn’t it? It’s for everyone, everywhere,” Infantino told reporters in Warri yesterday. “It’s big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also smaller stadiums. It’s the proximity, and to be here in Warri for me is a fantastic occasion to showcase what we are about in FIFA, what we are about in football.” Infantino also expressed appreciation for the warm reception he received in Nigeria and across Africa, attributing the relationship to years of collaboration and football development projects aimed at improving the lives of young people. “Oh yes, I’m feeling so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. This is based, of course, on many years of joint life together, of projects that we’ve put in place, of changing lives of girls and boys,” he said. nigeria.title: Lagos renews campaign against open defecation
nigeria.description: …Calls for improved sanitation, gender-sensitive toilet facilities By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has renewed its campaign for improved sanitation, proper hygiene practices and access to safe toilet facilities as part of efforts to eliminate open defecation and promote public health. The Special Adviser to the Governor on Environment, Olakunle Akodu, and the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Tajudeen Gaji, made the call on Friday as the state joined the rest of the world to commemorate World Toilet Day at Alausa, Ikeja. The 2026 celebration was held under the theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality.” Akodu said women and girls required toilet facilities that guaranteed adequate privacy, reliable water supply, handwashing stations and hygienic conditions. He noted that Lagos’ growing population, rapid urbanisation and expanding commercial activities had placed enormous pressure on existing sanitation infrastructure. According to him, addressing the challenges requires deliberate public policies, sustained capital investment, institutional discipline and collective civic responsibility. He said the state government recognised that a clean, resilient and sustainable environment must guarantee every resident access to safe, dignified and functional sanitation facilities. Earlier, Gaji, who was represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Hassan Sanuth, said the commemoration underscored the importance of proper sanitation in preventing diseases, protecting public health and promoting a cleaner environment. He described access to safe toilets as more than a basic necessity, saying it was fundamental to human dignity and public health. Gaji said sanitation was closely linked to personal security, social equality and the fundamental right of every citizen to live in a healthy environment. He warned that inadequate access to safe and private toilet facilities could undermine people’s health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. The permanent secretary therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that would address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. nigeria.description: …Warns staff against laxity, promises operational overhaul By Olasunkanmi Akoni The newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to tackle waste management challenges across Lagos State, warning staff against indiscipline and poor performance. Akinyemi, who has assumed office amid growing concerns over waste accumulation across the metropolis, said the plan was aimed at clearing waste backlogs, strengthening regulatory enforcement and restoring the agency’s operational efficiency. He disclosed this on Friday while addressing management and staff at a workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa, Lagos. Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Kunle Adebiyi, the acting managing director called for renewed commitment, discipline and professionalism among workers. He said repositioning the agency would require active participation and dedication from personnel at all levels. “We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. “We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi said. Outlining the 60-day action plan, he said personnel would be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with the respective areas to strengthen field monitoring and improve response times. He also announced plans to establish decentralised operational hubs to improve supervision, facilitate faster interventions and address waste disposal blackspots across the state. On indiscriminate waste disposal, Akinyemi said the agency would intensify public enlightenment on waste sorting at source and responsible disposal practices. He said traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations and artisans would be mobilised to promote compliance with proper waste management practices. The acting managing director also called for stronger collaboration with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and urged residents to comply with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain service delivery. On staff welfare, Akinyemi assured workers that their well-being remained a priority, disclosing that efforts were underway to procure Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered buses to address transportation challenges. Earlier, Tijani called for urgent action to revitalise LAWMA’s operational framework, saying the agency needed an immediate overhaul to improve field performance. nigeria.title: CONTTA: Varsity health workers petition education minister over NSIWC exclusion
nigeria.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou The Coalition of Healthcare Professionals in Tertiary Education Institutions of Nigeria, CHPTEIN, has petitioned the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, demanding the suspension of a circular issued by the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission,NSIWC allegedly excluding healthcare workers in federal universities from the payment of the Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Teaching Allowance, CONTTA. The coalition, representing affected medical doctors, nurses, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists and other allied health professionals under the Consolidated Health Salary Structure, CONHESS and Consolidated Medical Salary Structure, CONMESS, also faulted widespread media reports describing the CONTTA payments as “excess payments” and subject to recovery. In an emergency petition delivered to the minister on Thursday, November 19, 2026, CHPTEIN rejected the characterisation, insisting that the payments were based on verified payroll computations by the Budget Office of the Federation and covered all eligible non-teaching staff in federal universities, irrespective of union affiliation. The petition challenged NSIWC Circular Ref: SWC/S/04/S.149/T/187, dated November 11, 2026, which the coalition said unlawfully excluded CONHESS and CONMESS healthcare workers from the CONTTA payment arrangement. Copies of the petition were also served on the Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi; the Director-General of the Budget Office of the Federation; and the Chairman of NSIWC. The coalition argued that the November 11 circular directly contradicted an earlier directive by the Federal Ministry of Education, dated October 16, 2026, with reference number FME/TE/SS.IM/C./Vol.I/6. According to CHPTEIN, the ministry’s directive explicitly confirmed that the Budget Office of the Federation calculated the financial implications of CONTTA based on the entire workforce of non-teaching staff on the payroll, covering the payment of allowances to all non-teaching staff irrespective of their union affiliation. The coalition quoted the ministry’s clarification as stating: “The Budget Office of the Federation calculated the financial implications of CONTTA based on the entire workforce of the Non-teaching staff on the payroll… covering the payment of allowances of all Non-teaching staff irrespective of their union affiliation.” It questioned how NSIWC could unilaterally override the position of the supervising ministry, particularly when the funds had already been budgeted and released for all non-teaching workers on the nominal roll. nigeria.title: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal
nigeria.description: A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll will not be repeated. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023. ﻿ He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest. “Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he maintained. The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, while defeating former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa. “I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria. “Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added. On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency. Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option. Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considers a more effective means of engaging voters. He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence. “First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added. Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”. The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow. Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agric,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agric. Is that wrong? business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function. The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers. How SHRINCS works SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both. Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block. The risk of a stateful signature The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size. Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.” Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. entertainment.description: The role of home appliances is changing. Today’s consumers expect more than products that simply perform everyday tasks. They want solutions that are intuitive, efficient and capable of making daily life easier. Across Africa, rapid urbanisation, changing lifestyles and growing digital adoption are reshaping consumer expectations. Homeowners are increasingly seeking appliances that combine convenience, performance, energy efficiency and intelligent functionality while fitting seamlessly into their everyday routines. In response, LG Electronics continues to develop innovations that place people at the centre of technology. Guided by its vision for smarter, more connected living, the company is introducing solutions that help consumers spend less time on household chores and more time on what matters most. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. sports.title: 5 takeaways from Oregon Ducks stylish 45-7 blowout over Michigan State
sports.description: It was a game that the Oregon Ducks needed to win, and needed to look good doing so. They did just that. Dan Lanning's team got its first ever victory in East Lansing on Friday night, beating the Michigan State Spartans 45-7 in a game that really was ugly early on, but dominated in the second half. Spurred on by a fake field goal that went for a touchdown right before the break, Oregon scored 35 points over the final 30 minutes and seven seconds of the game, and put up some style points in the eyes of the College Football Playoff committee, which may have been the most important outcome of it all. The defense was dominant once again, while true freshman running back Brandon Smith stepped in for an injured Dierre Hill and had a coming-out party. Now, with a full day of college football ahead of us on Saturday, we will sit back and see how things unfold for the Ducks . Before that, though, here are our biggest takeaways from the game: Style Points Coming into this game, there was a notion that winning wasn't going to be enough for Oregon; the Ducks needed to win with style. Sitting on the outside of the College Football Playoff field looking in, an impressive showing was needed in order to help convince the committee that Oregon is playing as one of the best 12 teams in the nation right now, and deserving of a shot at the national championship. I think they accomplished that. It didn't look pretty for much of the first two quarters, with Oregon putting up only 166 yards and 10 points before a gutsy fake field goal at the end of the half. But over the final 30 minutes and seven seconds of football, the Ducks were dominant. They ended up with 422 total yards and 45 points, letting some of their most dynamic players — mainly RB Brandon Smith and WR Dakorien Moore — show what they could do while the defense was dominant once again. A lot of things can happen in order to clear the Ducks' path to the playoffs, and we may see some of them come to fruition on Saturday, but even if some upsets don't take place, there's a reason to believe that Oregon might be able to get in at 9-3. Games like this one certainly help build the case. The Brandon Smith Game Without Dierre Hill for a majority of this game (more on that later), this quickly turned into the Brandon Smith game for the Ducks. Oregon fans knew before this game that they had something special in the true freshman, but he cemented that fact in this one, rushing 14 times for 121 yards and two touchdowns. It wasn't just the stats, but the way that he ran, shifting through contact, maintaining elite balance, and dancing down the sideline on impressive big gains. He looked good enough to get legendary Oregon RB Jonathan Stewart to make this statement: "Brandon Smith the best back in a Oregon jersey since Kenjon Barner." — @Jonathanstewar1 https://t.co/lxrIEzV7QT — Zachary Neel (@zacharycneel) November 21, 2026 Whether you agree with Stewart or not is beside the point. sports.description: Michigan State’s Derrick Simmons, left, tackles Oregon’s Da'Jaun Riggs during the first quarter on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026 in East Lansing. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Whew, boy. That was the worst loss of the season. It was all Oregon tonight. Michigan State’s offense struggled early, and Oregon scored halfway through the first quarter to give the Ducks a 7-0 lead behind a Brandon Smith 5-yard touchdown run. Frederick Moore had a nice one-handed snag right before the second quarter started, but Liam Boyd would miss a 47-yard field goal for Michigan State’s first chance to put points on the board. The offense was starting to look solid behind Kayd Coffman’s play, but he would trip while running out of the pocket to turn the ball over on a 4th-and-3 from Oregon’s 28-yard line. The defense did their best to keep the Spartans close, but their special teams did not. Chrishon McCray would muff the next punt by the Ducks to allow Oregon to take over in the redzone. The defense held tough and forced them to kick a field goal, and it made it a 10-0 game. Near the end of the first half, Dan Lanning called a fake field goal where the Ducks’ kicker was able to run it in from 15 yards out to give Oregon a 17-0 lead heading into halftime. Once that fake field goal scored, it felt like the game was already out of reach. Oregon opened up the second half with another touchdown run, this time from Simeon Price, to put them up 24-0. Michigan State would respond with a touchdown of their own with a direct snap from the 1-yard line by Jaz Patterson, though it would be the only points they scored all night. Both Brandon Smith and Simeon Price would add another touchdown run each for the Ducks, and Dylan Raiola found Dakorien Moore for a nice one-handed touchdown pass as Oregon continued to pile on the points. Oregon would go on to win 45 to 7. Michigan State moves to 3-8 Kayd Coffman completed 10 of his 19 passes for 106 yards and one interception. Jaz Patterson handled 16 carries, but only managed 26 yards. Brandon Tullis added 25 yards on eight carries. The Spartans’ leading receiver was Fredrick Moore with 31 yards on two catches. It was a brutal loss, and one of those games where you wish it could’ve ended by the end of the third quarter, as Oregon kept putting more and more points on the scoreboard. Luckily for the Spartans, it’s not the end of the season, and they’ll finish it off with a matchup at Rutgers on Thanksgiving weekend. Let’s hope they can finish the season with a win. Go Green!
